reasoning: توقّع is fully colloquialised, so both ق are glottal stops (compare متوقع mitwa''i3). heek is written with kasra plus ya for the long ee.
An everyday word in Ramallah, so ق glottalises: il-musta'bal.
MSA-origin verbal noun used normally in school and work talk. Taa marbuta after ك is e.
ع shortens to 3a and the article assimilates to the sun letter ز. The medial i drops: zaawye, with taa marbuta e after ي.
Literally the daughter of the mother's brother, so a maternal female cousin. Plain construct, no linking vowel after بنت.
ق is a glottal stop and the final cluster takes an epenthetic vowel: 3a'il. With a suffix the vowel disappears again: 3a'lo.
The first vowel is kept here because w- plus 7 is hard to cluster. The word also means 'only / sole'; for 'lonely' Ramallah speakers often say حاسس حالي لحالي.
Urban Palestinian has no ذ in inherited words, so it is respelled د: idin, idni 'my ear'. ودن widin is also widely heard.
ط is emphatic T. عافية loses its medial vowel and ends in e: 3aafye. Standard reply to someone working.
With kasra on the ر it is the active participle 'importer', as the English says; with fatha the same spelling is mustawrad 'imported'. Business register but genuinely used.
Geminate final b from the shadda. The everyday Palestinian word for a young man; plural shabaab.
Palestinian i-i vocalism in this stative past tense, miriD, not MSA mariDa. ض is emphatic D.
biddi is the Palestinian 'I want' and ق in قهوة is a glottal stop. Both taa marbutas are e, after و and after د.
ح is not in the list that settles the taa marbuta, but the pharyngeal keeps the vowel open here, so saa7a. This is the normal Palestinian word for a town square.
The -iyya suffix is -iyye in Palestinian, with shadda on the ي. Political vocabulary used normally in Ramallah.
Without the initial alif the word begins in a cluster: wlaad, the variant of awlaad. Means children or boys.
The imperfect of وجع has a long uu stem, yuuja3, and b- is prefixed before it. راس, not رأس, is the Palestinian word.
ما negates the verb, as Palestinian requires. ق is a glottal stop and ط is emphatic: ti'Ta3. Literally 'don't cut yourself off from us'.
Denominal verb from kaff 'palm', geminate: kaffo 'he slapped him'. The same spelling is also the noun 'palm of the hand'.
ذ in this inherited root is د in urban Palestinian (kidib 'he lied'), so it is respelled. Taa marbuta after ب is e.
Loanword with two short vowels; no gemination in Palestinian speech despite the English spelling.
Long oo, not uu. Taa marbuta after the back consonant خ is a.
An English loan, so the p is kept as a Latin letter; speakers who lack p say briinter. The MSA word طابعة is not used in conversation.
Palestinian drops the first short vowel, unlike Egyptian gineeh. Long ee before the final h.
Taa marbuta after ب is e. The word covers both 'experience' and 'experiment / trial' in Palestinian use.
